blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Long-term assistants must follow unfinished tasks across days as information and circumstances change. Finding information or starting an action, however, does not ensure that the task gets completed. We introduce OptionWorld, a benchmark that traces information acquisition, judgments, actions, and outcomes in simulated daily-life tasks to identify where current LLMs fall short as long-term personal assistants. In runs with archived decision inputs, the key facts remain in the model's last input before the deadline in 35.5% of failed instances. Failure analysis identifies the three most frequent problems: needed information is not obtained or combined, available opportunities to act go unused, and agents impose restrictions that the task does not require. Three follow-up experiments show that supplying missing facts restores task success in some cases; action reminders can restart work while subsequent steps still miss the deadline; and correcting a supplied note that wrongly forbids contact restores permitted inquiry. These findings locate shortcomings in maintaining task state: connecting facts to unfinished work, following through before deadlines, and separating actual restrictions from the agent's assumptions.
blocks.zh: 随着信息和情况的变化,长期助理必须日复一日地执行未完成的任务。 然而,寻找信息或采取行动并不能确保任务完成。 我们引入了OptionWorld,这个基准在模拟的日常生活任务中追溯信息获取,判断,行动和结果,以识别当前LLMS作为长期个人助理的不足之处. 在有存档决定投入的情况下,关键事实在35.5%的失败事例中仍保留在模型截止日期前的最后投入中。 失败分析查明了三个最常见的问题:没有获得或合并所需信息,没有利用现有行动机会,特工人员施加任务不需要的限制。 3项后续实验显示,提供缺失的事实在某些情况下恢复了任务的成功;行动提醒可以重新开始工作,而随后的步骤仍然错过最后期限;并纠正所提供的错误地禁止联系的注释恢复了允许的调查。 这些调查结果找出了在维持任务状态方面的缺点:将事实与未完成的工作联系起来,在最后期限之前完成,并将实际限制与代理人的假设分开。

The problem: sustaining follow-through. LLM agents use language models to choose actions through tools, such as
reading records or contacting people ( Yao et al., 2023 ) .
Agents also retain memories and reflections ( Packer et al., 2023 ; Shinn et al., 2023 ) .
As long-term personal assistants,
they must follow unfinished work as information, deadlines, and user needs
change. For example, an insurer may report an unpaid premium despite an
earlier bank receipt (Figure 1 ). The assistant must connect
the records, follow updated permission to consult both parties, and complete
the user-approved action before the deadline. Maintaining task state means tracking unfinished work, permitted next steps, and
their deadlines. We ask where current LLMs fall short in this responsibility
and what support helps them resume progress.

blocks.en:
Our approach: locating where tasks stall. Existing benchmarks examine task execution, memory, and proactive
assistance ( Zhou et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2025 ; Wu et al., 2026 ; Pasternak et al., 2025 ; Studio and AI, 2026 ) .
Task and stage scores alone, however, leave open whether a failed target
lacked necessary facts, retained those facts without using them effectively,
or stalled during subsequent action. Distinguishing these problems requires
connecting outcomes to the information and decisions behind them. We introduce OptionWorld , a benchmark of simulated insurance, work, housing, and other
ongoing matters. Agents discover needs through daily events and records
without seeing the evaluation targets. For each target, we connect fact
acquisition, the facts still visible at decision time, judgments, actions,
and outcomes across days to locate where progress stops.

blocks.en:
Main findings: information is only part of the problem. The three most frequent problems concern connecting facts to unfinished
work and updating next steps: missing or unassembled
information, unused follow-ups or retries, and restrictions the agent adds
without a basis in the task. The fact-acquisition analysis finds that
nearly half of failures occur after
the primary facts were obtained in time. In runs with archived inputs,
over one-third of failures still have those facts in the last valid
decision input. Failure therefore extends beyond information acquisition.
Cross-day records help explain how obstacles develop: one agent saves a
rejection as a requirement to wait for another record and continues waiting
days later, although the rejection never imposed that condition. Here,
memory preserves a mistaken interpretation that guides later inaction.

blocks.en: 3 Benchmark and Evaluation Design
blocks.zh: 3 基准和评价设计

blocks.en: 3.1 Worlds and Interaction
blocks.zh: 3.1 世界与互动

blocks.en:
OptionWorld contains eight authored daily-life simulations spanning housing, work,
independent living, and family coordination. A target is a specific
issue to discover and address. Each 60-day world contains 24 targets,
totaling 192. Agents receive broad responsibilities, so they must discover
these needs from events and records without seeing the target list.
Evaluator-only specifications define required evidence, response periods,
and success conditions. Tasks may require comparing records across sources
or days, noticing that expected events have not occurred, or seeking
clarification or authorization.

blocks.en:
To locate where progress stops, we score the outcome and the preceding
evidence, judgments, and actions. Success requires feedback confirming that
the agent preserved a choice the user would otherwise lose or resolved the
issue. For example, confirmed protection of a pending clinic pickup
preserves an option; an accepted inquiry alone does not establish that outcome.

even the highest-scoring system leaves more than one-third unfinished.

blocks.en:
Astra has lower source-access coverage than DeepSeek (85.1% versus 96.5%)
and has similar timely grounded discovery (77.8% versus 78.1%), yet
delivers more interventions (68.6% versus 57.1%) and completes more
targets. Source access records whether at least one relevant source was
accessed, rather than the amount of information gathered. To compare
follow-through on the same tasks, we match 275 instances for which both
systems make timely grounded judgments and have no uncertain stage labels.

reconsidering what to do when a temporary obstacle
disappears, not merely preserving the unfinished task
(Appendix L ).

Less frequent problems are state or updating errors (6.4%) and execution
errors (2.0%). A scan of shared-runner trajectories shows that state
maintenance also requires stopping completed operations: 69 target instances
in 33 trajectories incur 106

targets are successful under the rubric, so success rates alone miss this
redundant activity. The pattern is concentrated in Gemini (59 instances):
one trajectory executes on Day 6, receives completion feedback on Day 7,
then reuses the same authorization on Days 7, 9, and 13.
Together with the missed-retry case, this reveals two
directions of state error: leaving a temporary block in place and failing
to retire a completed step. Execution errors instead concern parameters, object bindings,
or operation order that block an action .

blocks.en: 6 Discussion and Conclusion

blocks.en:
OptionWorld locates shortcomings in long-term assistance by connecting each
unfinished target to its evidence, judgments, actions, and outcome.
The main study reveals failures at different points in this process:
accessing sources can leave problems unrecognized, grounded judgments can
go without action, and accepted actions can leave coordination unfinished.
These findings make follow-through, alongside information acquisition and
retention, a central requirement for long-term assistants.

The primary label identifies the documented obstacle still blocking the
target. When several problems appear, an explicit unsupported prerequisite
can explain subsequent inaction, while a repaired parameter error does not
displace a remaining obstacle. Each instance receives one primary label;
the five problem types are: • Self-restriction: an unsupported prerequisite or expanded
prohibition is explicitly used to wait, refuse, or restrict progress. • State or updating error: a wrong matter, date, source, or
status is used in a decision, or a superseded judgment continues to govern it. • Action selection or adjustment: the record establishes a
permitted opportunity, but the agent fails to take the available action,
retry, follow up, or try another approach. • Execution error: an identifiable agent-side parameter,
binding, ordering, or procedure error obstructs the selected operation and
remains relevant to progress. • Information gap: needed facts are not obtained, assembled,
or retained in time, without evidence for a more specific primary problem.

blocks.en:
In Run 2 of the returning-to-work caregiver world, both systems inspect a claimant
commitment allowing 24 hours of availability on Day 3 and a portal
assignment of 35 search hours on Day 7. Both recognize the conflict.
Astra requests confirmation on Day 7 to submit a correction request,
while preserving both records and leaving factual reconciliation to the
responsible record holder. It executes the confirmed action on Day 8;
Day-9 environment feedback confirms option preservation, not resolution
of the conflicting records. DeepSeek saves the discrepancy and registers
a watchpoint on Day 7, waiting for the record holder to become available,
but delivers no qualifying intervention for this target.
The difference is how recognized uncertainty guides the next step:
Astra uses an authorized protective action without claiming to have
settled the facts; DeepSeek retains the conflict as a monitoring condition.
The archived target is risk-caregiver_returning_to_work-01-02 .
Evidence appears at Astra trace indices 17, 41, 44, 49, and 56, and
DeepSeek indices 24, 61, 71, and 72; indices are zero-based in the Run-2
traces mapped by main_manifest.json in the reproduction archive.

blocks.en:
Both setups have a harness : the execution framework that supplies
context, dispatches tools, and returns feedback to the model.
The common runner starts a new conversation each day, carrying saved
memory and watchpoints; Astra uses the local Codex agent interface.
Codex’s documented harness manages conversation state and tool execution
across turns ( Bonamy and Choi, 2026 ) .
This makes continuity of pending steps and use of action feedback plausible
contributors to follow-through. The observed comparison changes both the
model and its harness, so it describes their combined behavior. A
same-model comparison across harnesses would isolate whether these
execution features improve follow-through; the case above identifies
concrete behaviors to test: turning a recognized conflict into an
authorized action and checking its outcome.

blocks.en:
The companion optionworld_recovery archive contains all 39
information/action continuations, 78 accepted AI review contexts, checkpoint
states, screening records, protocols, and offline replay and scoring code.
Public copies redact machine paths and opaque provider signatures, with
both original and distributed-file hashes recorded in the index. They
support simulator replay and score reproduction; signature-dependent
provider requests require the originals.

blocks.en:
The archive provides a route from an explicit world snapshot to a new
trace, identity-masked review packet,
paired review import, and the same six-criterion scorer. It reuses the
public-input packer, tool schemas, runtime, and scoring functions. An offline
mock exercises all eight worlds. New runs remain separate from the archived
campaign. The accompanying documentation gives model configuration,
review steps, and request and cost controls.

审查步骤、请求和费用控制。
